---
title: "Public API reference"
---

All objects below are exported from `metis`. Python docstrings describe their
arguments and exceptions. Hydra constructs these same objects.

| Object or method | Contract |
|---|---|
| `SimulationDataset.from_parquet(path, inputs=..., outputs=..., groups=None, time="t", replicate="rep")` | Read and validate complete numeric trajectories |
| `SimulationDataset.from_frame(frame, ...)` | Equivalent input from a pandas or Polars frame |
| `SimulationDataset.from_arrays(inputs, outputs, input_names=..., output_names=..., ...)` | Numeric arrays with shapes `(N,P)` and `(N,T,C)` |
| `bank.split(validation_fraction=.2, test_fraction=.2, seed=42)` | Disjoint scenario partitions; zero fractions disable optional partitions |
| `DatasetSplit.from_datasets(train, validation=None, test=None)` | Validate supplied partitions and reject overlap |
| `Surrogate(model="mlp", model_options=None)` | Select family and optional architecture overrides; data dimensions inferred |
| `surrogate.fit(train, validation=None, config=TrainingConfig(...), on_progress=None)` | Fit training-only scales and weights, restore best validation weights; optional callback receives a copy of each progress record |
| `surrogate.predict(inputs, ...)` | Original-unit deterministic prediction `(B,T,C)`; stochastic mean requires explicit `n_samples` |
| `surrogate.sample(inputs, n_samples=100, seed=42, num_steps=50, solver="heun")` | Stochastic samples `(B,S,T,C)`; ODE settings apply to flow matching |
| `surrogate.evaluate(bank, ...)` | `EvaluationReport` with original-unit metrics and provenance |
| `surrogate.save(path)` / `Surrogate.load(path, device="cpu")` | Complete versioned artifact, independent of source data |
| `surrogate.log_prob(inputs, outputs)` | iTARFlow continuous log density, original units |
| `surrogate.log_prob_tensor(inputs, outputs)` | Differentiable iTARFlow log density |
| `assess_coverage(training, candidates)` | Marginal range flags and distance to existing inputs |
| `suggest_simulations(training, candidates, n=10)` | Greedy coverage suggestions over supplied candidates |
| `load_example()` | Bundled 100-group, 40-timepoint SIRDS subset |

`TrainingConfig` defaults: steps=500, batch_size=64, learning_rate=0.001,
weight_decay=0.001, seed=42, device="cpu", eval_every=50, patience=None.
The package training loop uses constant-learning-rate AdamW and optional
validation patience. This is distinct from the historical source trainer's
warm-up/cosine schedule. Configure and report the workflow actually used.

The public pipeline supports CPU and CUDA in float32. It does not automatically
select precision, compile the model, run distributed training, enforce physical
constraints or choose a model family. Advanced model classes remain importable
from `metis.models`; historical CUDA/DDP recipes remain available in the checkout.

Optional tracking is available as `from metis.tracking import WandbTracker`.
Use its context manager and pass `on_progress=tracker.log_training` to `fit`.
The core library never requires a W&B account; tracking can also run offline.
